## Vocabulary

- **self**: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening (16/3)

## How it works

- [statement] Do not accept client-controlled JavaScript or raw query objects. Build application-owned filters with driver APIs, validate expected value types, and allowlist fields and operators. JavaScript interpolation can enable data extraction, while client-supplied objects can introduce operators even when the application uses query objects. (high confidence) — https://portswigger.net/web-security/nosql-injection · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/NoSQL_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html
- [statement] Percona's June 17, 2026 advisory describes CVE-2026-11933 in the older BSON-to-JavaScript-array conversion path: an authenticated user with read privileges and scripting enabled could trigger memory disclosure or a crash. Its upstream ticket concerns BSON wrapper ownership. This historical evidence does not establish that MongoDB 9.0's WASM engine has the same vulnerability. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-17) — https://www.percona.com/blog/security-advisory-cve-2026-9740-and-cve-2026-11933-in-percona-server-for-mongodb/ · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-128125

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Prefer native aggregation expressions inside $expr over $where when they express the same predicate. Replacing $where with $expr plus $function still executes JavaScript and still requires scripting to be enabled. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/function.md · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md
- [statement] Prefer native aggregation expressions, including through $expr, over $where when they express the same logic. If custom JavaScript is necessary, MongoDB prefers $function over $where; moving JavaScript under $expr does not eliminate JavaScript execution. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/function.md · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] $function uses a body containing JavaScript, an args array, and lang: "js" to define a custom aggregation expression. MongoDB recommends it only when native pipeline operators cannot fulfill the application's needs, because JavaScript execution may reduce performance. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/function.md · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md
- [statement] $where itself cannot use indexes, and a $where-only filter requires a collection scan. If it cannot be removed, include ordinary selective predicates: MongoDB evaluates non-$where conditions first, and those conditions may use indexes. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/where.md · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening
- [statement] If the application does not require $where, $function, $accumulator, or mapReduce, disable server-side scripting on mongod and mongos using security.javascriptEnabled: false or --noscripting. Inventory application queries before disabling because dependent operations will fail. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/server-side-javascript.md · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/function.md, https://www.percona.com/blog/security-advisory-cve-2026-9740-and-cve-2026-11933-in-percona-server-for-mongodb/, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/NoSQL_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html
- [statement] MongoDB 8.0 deprecated $function, $accumulator, and $where and logged warnings when they ran; deprecation did not mean immediate removal. (high confidence) (verified as of 2024-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/core/server-side-javascript/ · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/why-is-function-deprecated-in-mongod-8-0/291213
- [statement] MongoDB 9.0 reverses the MongoDB 8.0 deprecation of $function, $accumulator, and $where. Do not carry an unqualified "deprecated since 8.0" recommendation into 9.0 guidance. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-28) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/9.0.md · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening
- [statement] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, ppc64le mongod and mongos binaries omit the JavaScript engine: $function, $accumulator, $where, and mapReduce fail there. A configuration switch cannot restore support; rewrite the operations or use an architecture with a JavaScript engine. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/server-side-javascript.md · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/9.0-compatibility.md
- [statement] MongoDB 8.0 deprecated $function, $accumulator, and $where and logs warnings when they execute. MongoDB 9.0 reverses that deprecation and re-enables these functions using a WASM-based engine; a blanket claim that they remain deprecated in every version after 8.0 is incorrect. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-28) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/core/server-side-javascript/ · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/9.0.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, server-side local Date operations use UTC instead of the mongod host time zone. Review $function date logic before upgrading; use native date operators with an explicit timezone, or explicit UTC JavaScript methods when UTC is intended. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/server-side-javascript.md · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/9.0-compatibility.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Disabling JavaScript does not eliminate NoSQL operator injection. Non-JavaScript operators such as $ne or $regex can still change filter semantics if the application accepts unvalidated query structures; field, type, and operator validation remains necessary. (high confidence) — https://portswigger.net/web-security/nosql-injection · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/NoSQL_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html
- [statement] MongoDB attributes stronger sandboxing and isolation in 9.0 to its WASM-based JavaScript engine. This is an engine-hardening claim, not evidence that accepting untrusted query operators or JavaScript bodies becomes safe; application input validation is still necessary. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/9.0.md · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/9.0-compatibility.md, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/NoSQL_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html
- [statement] A 2024 community discussion reports workloads where custom JavaScript outperformed native aggregation rewrites, including IP transformations. Treat these as workload-specific reports, not a transferable benchmark or proof that JavaScript is universally faster. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/why-is-function-deprecated-in-mongod-8-0/291213 · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening
- [statement] $function requires server-side scripting, which MongoDB documents as enabled by default. Do not assume installation defaults have already disabled JavaScript; inspect the configuration of the deployed version. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/function.md · keywords: $function and server-side JavaScript hardening
